_note: ADR 0010 (T1-03) — worked solutions to battery v2, solved straight by the subscription model (measuring_model_id below). The fixed detector (atlas.distance.detect_methods) scans these for which node signatures actually appear — behavioral, never a self-report. Solved without consulting the signature list or the held-out pairs while writing.

solutions.p01: The temperature obeys the diffusion (heat) equation dT/dt = a*d2T/dx2. Expand the profile in a Fourier sine series matching the boundary conditions; each Fourier mode decays at a rate set by its eigenvalue, so high-frequency components vanish fastest and the profile relaxes toward the steady state where dT/dt = 0 (a linear gradient).
solutions.p02: Linearize the dynamics about the upright equilibrium, which is an unstable fixed point. Design a feedback controller: measure the angle error from vertical and apply a corrective cart force proportional to that error signal and its derivative. Choosing the loop gain so the closed loop has poles with negative real parts stabilizes the equilibrium.
solutions.p03: Use the sample mean as the estimate and the standard error s/sqrt(n) for the uncertainty (a confidence interval). Equivalently, put a prior on the population mean and update it with the sample likelihood to obtain a posterior; the posterior spread is the uncertainty (Bayes).
solutions.p04: Model the cities as nodes of a complete weighted graph and seek the shortest Hamiltonian cycle. Exact search is intractable, so use a heuristic under a length objective (the fitness): start from a tour and iteratively improve it, or evolve a set of random tours, keeping the fitter ones and applying mutation.
solutions.p05: The circular orbit is a fixed point of the radial equation (gravity balancing the centrifugal term). Linearize about it: the Jacobian / effective-potential curvature determines stability — the orbit is stable if small perturbations oscillate (real restoring eigenvalues) rather than grow.
solutions.p06: Write the logistic rate equation dN/dt = rN(1 - N/K). Setting dN/dt = 0 gives the steady states N=0 and the carrying capacity N=K; linearizing shows N=K is the stable equilibrium the population approaches over time.
solutions.p07: Transform the image with a Fourier (or wavelet) basis and suppress the high-frequency noise spectrum while keeping the dominant low-frequency structure; inverting reconstructs a cleaner image. Equivalently solve a maximum-entropy / regularized reconstruction that is least-biased subject to fidelity to the data.
solutions.p08: Model the asset price as a stochastic process and price the option as the discounted expected payoff. Estimate that expectation by Monte Carlo: simulate many random price paths, average the payoffs; the variance of the estimate falls with the number of draws.
solutions.p09: Write forward and reverse rate equations for the reacting species. Setting the net rate to zero gives the equilibrium concentrations (the steady state where forward equals reverse), fixed by the equilibrium constant.
solutions.p10: Represent individuals as nodes on a graph, each updating toward neighbors' opinions. The dynamics can reach a consensus fixed point or polarize; whether one opinion takes over is a tipping / percolation phenomenon — a phase transition in adoption as the coupling crosses a critical value (high-centrality nodes accelerate it).
solutions.p11: Reduce the high-dimensional feature matrix with PCA (the leading eigenvectors / principal components of the covariance), then cluster patients in the resulting low-dimensional latent space into a few subtypes, choosing the grouping that best separates them under a within-cluster objective.
solutions.p12: Use kinetic theory: pressure is the momentum flux of molecules striking the wall. Take the maximum-entropy (Maxwell-Boltzmann) velocity distribution consistent with the mean energy — obtained by maximizing entropy subject to the energy constraint via a Lagrange multiplier — to recover PV = NkT.
solutions.p13: Use feedback control: compare actual speed to the setpoint and apply throttle proportional to the error plus its integral, so steady disturbances like hills are rejected. Tune the loop gain for a stable closed loop that holds the setpoint.
solutions.p14: With a limited budget over a huge mutation space, treat it as search under constraint: evaluate candidate mutations for activity (fitness), keep the best, and propose new variants by mutation and recombination (directed evolution). Iterating this selection-and-variation improves activity within the budget.
